intro: A book can tell you what to believe. It can also tell you how to live. The Qur'an does both. This unit looks at what the Qur'an teaches: about one God, about being honest and kind, and about what Muslims do each day and each year because of it.

You will meet a wise man named Luqman and his seven pieces of advice. You will read what the Qur'an says about parents, promises, orphans and boasting. Then you will follow a Muslim child's day and year: the five daily prayers, giving, the month of Ramadan, the journey to Mecca and the two Eid holidays.

Every time, you will see where in the Qur'an an idea comes from, by surah and ayah. You will say "Muslims believe" and "the Qur'an says," so you can describe a faith fairly, whether it is yours or not. By the end you will be able to explain each of the Five Pillars and the verses Muslims point to for them.
bigQuestion: What does the Qur'an ask of Muslims, in belief and in daily life, and where in the book does each teaching come from?

timeline.t: Muhammad is born in Mecca, according to Muslim tradition
Muslims believe the first words of the Qur'an come to Muhammad in a cave
Muhammad begins to teach in Mecca: one God, care for the poor and orphans
The hijra to Medina; the Muslim calendar begins from this year
Muslims begin to face Mecca in prayer and to fast in Ramadan, as tradition tells it
Muhammad returns to Mecca and the Kaaba is cleared of its statues
The farewell pilgrimage and sermon; Muhammad dies in Medina
The Qur'an is gathered into one standard written copy, as Muslim tradition tells it
Al-Bukhari and Muslim collect hadith, including the list of the Five Pillars
Islam is presented at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago
Marmaduke Pickthall publishes his English translation of the Qur'an
About 1.9 billion Muslims (estimates vary) pray, fast and give around the world

words.d: the belief that there is only one God; the Qur'an's central idea
one line or verse of the Qur'an; a surah is a whole chapter
the line "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" that opens nearly every surah
a wise man in the Qur'an who gave his son advice; Surah 31 is named for him
a child whose parents have died; the Qur'an says to care for orphans
the day Muslims believe every person will answer to God for what they did
one of the five main practices of Islam: shahada, prayer, zakat, fasting and hajj
the statement of faith: there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God
the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face when they pray
a share of savings that Muslims give each year to people in need
the ninth month of the Muslim calendar, when Muslims fast from dawn to sunset
allowed; food and actions that Muslims may have or do

choices: The belief that there is only one God
test.why: Tawhid is the Qur'an's central idea: there is only one God.

test.q: Which surah do Muslims say sums up the idea of one God in four short ayahs?
test.why: Surah 112, Al-Ikhlas, says God is one, needs nothing, has no children and has no equal.

test.q: What do Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim, the names in the Bismillah, mean?
choices: The Most Gracious and the Most Merciful
test.why: Both names come from the root for mercy: the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

test.q: In Surah 17:23, what rule comes right after worshiping one God?
test.why: 17:23 puts kindness to parents right after worship of one God.

test.q: What was the FIRST piece of advice Luqman gave his son?
choices: Do not set up partners with God
test.why: 31:13 begins with the biggest idea: there is one God, and setting up partners with God is a great wrong.

test.q: What does Surah 2:177 say a good person does?
choices: Gives money to relatives, orphans, the poor and travelers, and keeps promises
test.why: 2:177 lists giving to those in need, praying, keeping promises and being patient.

test.q: Which angel do Muslims believe brought the words of the Qur'an to Muhammad?
test.why: Muslims believe Jibril (Gabriel), named in 2:97, brought the Qur'an's words over about 23 years.

test.q: How does the Qur'an describe paradise in 2:25?
test.why: 2:25 describes gardens with rivers flowing beneath and fruit.

test.q: Which list gives the Five Pillars?
test.why: The Five Pillars are the shahada, daily prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan and the hajj.

test.q: What does Surah 2:144 tell Muslims to do?
choices: Turn their faces toward the Sacred Mosque in Mecca when they pray
test.why: 2:144 sets the qibla: face the Sacred Mosque in Mecca in prayer.

test.q: Who does Surah 2:185 say may fast on other days instead of in Ramadan?
test.why: 2:185 says the sick and those on a journey may make up the fast on other days.

test.q: What does 3:97 say about the journey to the Kaaba?
choices: It must be made every Friday
It is only for people from Arabia
It is a duty for those who are able to make the trip
test.why: 3:97 says the journey to the House is a duty owed to God by those who can make it.

test.q: What is Eid al-Adha connected to?
choices: The end of the hajj and Ibrahim's readiness to give up his son
test.why: Eid al-Adha, the festival of the sacrifice, comes at the end of the hajj and remembers Ibrahim.

test.q: Which of these does Surah 2:173 say is NOT allowed to eat?
test.why: 2:173 forbids animals that died on their own, blood, pork and meat offered to idols.

test.q: Which sentence describes Muslims in the world today?
choices: All Muslims live in Arab countries
All Muslims speak Arabic at home
Most Muslims live in Asia, and Sunni and Shia Muslims share the Qur'an and the pillars
test.why: Most of the world's roughly 1.9 billion Muslims live in Asia and the Pacific; Sunni and Shia share the Qur'an and the pillars.

write.prompt: What does the Qur'an say a good person does? Pick two or three passages from this unit, such as 17:23–24 on parents, 2:177 on giving, 31:13–19 on Luqman's advice or 2:185 on fasting. For each, tell what the passage says in your own words, and how Muslims put it into practice.
tips: Name each passage by surah and ayah, like 2:177.
Say "the Qur'an says" or "Muslims believe" every time; describe, do not judge.
Use the unit's words: tawhid, zakat, qibla, Ramadan, halal.
Give one example of how a Muslim family might follow each passage.
Keep your sentences short and say one idea in each.
